note: Generic communication-behavior markers seen in harassment, stalking and threat cases. Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions. A match means the words appeared, not that the behavior was intended. Weight 1-5 drives the triage level only.

behaviors.name: Direct threat of violence
behaviors.description: States an intent to kill or physically harm the recipient or their family.
patterns: \b(?:i['’]?ll|i will|we['’]?ll|we will|i['’]?m going to|i am going to|i['’]?m gonna|i am gonna|im gonna|i gonna)\s+(?:kill|hurt|beat|shoot|stab|strangle|murder)\s+(?:you|u|your)\b
behaviors.legal_note: Written or electronic threats to kill or injure are addressed by Va. Code § 18.2-60. If you are in danger, call 911 first.

behaviors.name: Conditional threat or ultimatum
behaviors.description: Ties a harmful consequence to what the recipient does or refuses to do.
behaviors.legal_note: If something of value is demanded, extortion statutes (Va. Code § 18.2-59; 18 U.S.C. § 875(d)) may be relevant.

behaviors.name: Veiled or implied threat
behaviors.description: Menacing language that stops short of stating the harm.
behaviors.legal_note: Implied threats are harder to prosecute than explicit ones. Record exact words and context.

behaviors.name: Permanence declaration
behaviors.description: Says the contact will never end or cannot be escaped.
behaviors.legal_note: Statements of persistence can support a course-of-conduct showing in stalking cases (Va. Code § 18.2-60.3; 18 U.S.C. § 2261A).

behaviors.name: Surveillance or tracking claim
behaviors.description: Says the sender has been watching, tracking or knows where the recipient is.
behaviors.legal_note: Claims of tracking can show intent to cause fear. If the sender knows non-public details, check for account or device compromise.

behaviors.name: Threat to expose identifying information
behaviors.description: Threatens to publish an address, name, photos or other private information.
behaviors.legal_note: Publication with intent to harass is covered by Va. Code § 18.2-186.4. A threat alone may be analyzed under threat or extortion statutes.

behaviors.name: Demand for payment or compliance under threat
behaviors.description: Demands money, images or action and threatens exposure if refused.
behaviors.legal_note: Obtaining money or a benefit by threat can fall under Va. Code § 18.2-59.

behaviors.name: Coercive contact demand
behaviors.description: Insists the recipient respond, unblock or comply.
behaviors.legal_note: Repeated demands after a clear request to stop are relevant to course-of-conduct statutes.

behaviors.name: Contact after block or new accounts
behaviors.description: References being blocked, or contacts the recipient from new accounts.
behaviors.legal_note: Persistence after a block supports a pattern. A new account is not itself a crime.

behaviors.name: Rules-do-not-apply framing
behaviors.description: Claims immunity from rules, bans or consequences.
behaviors.legal_note: Defiance statements can help show willfulness after warnings.

behaviors.name: Blame-shifting or minimizing
behaviors.description: Puts responsibility on the recipient or dismisses the conduct.
behaviors.legal_note: Context-dependent and common in ordinary arguments. Weigh with other markers.

behaviors.name: Demeaning or diminutive address
behaviors.description: Condescending terms of address. Highly context-dependent; low confidence on its own.
behaviors.legal_note: Not unlawful by itself. Useful only as a repeated stylistic marker across messages.

behaviors.name: Claiming the recipient's identity
behaviors.description: States or implies the sender is the recipient or owns their images or history.
behaviors.legal_note: Identity statutes usually need an unlawful purpose or a benefit sought (Va. Code § 18.2-186.3; 18 U.S.C. § 1028(a)(7)). Document the purpose.

behaviors.name: Profane or vulgar language
behaviors.description: Profane or obscene words directed at the recipient.
behaviors.legal_note: Va. Code § 18.2-152.7:1 turns on obscene, vulgar or lewd content plus intent to coerce, intimidate or harass.
